titles.l2: Some things are not in a line

kernelIdea: Induction needs a statement indexed by integers n ≥ n₀ and a way to connect case k+1 back to case k. Statements about all real numbers are not candidates.

kernels.l1: Dominoes have to be in a line. Some things are not in a line.
kernels.l2: Dominoes only work if they are in a row, one after another. A claim about every number one at a time can be done with dominoes. A claim about everything at once cannot.
kernels.l3: Induction needs two things: cases lined up one after another, counted by whole numbers, and a way to get from one case to the next. A claim about every number on the number line has no next case, so induction cannot touch it.
kernels.l4: Induction requires a statement indexed by integers n ≥ n₀ and a link from case k to case k+1. Claims quantified over ℝ have no successor structure and are not candidates.
kernels.l5: Both requirements matter: an integer index and a usable link between consecutive cases; sums, products, and recursive definitions supply the link naturally.
kernels.l6: Where a statement is indexed by a well-ordered set with a successor, induction applies; strong induction and structural induction extend the method to other well-founded orders.
kernels.l7: Induction applies exactly when the statements are indexed by integers n ≥ n₀ and case k+1 is reachable from case k; without a successor structure — as over ℝ — the method does not apply at all.
kernels.l8: Induction is available on any well-founded order; strong induction, structural induction, and transfinite induction are the same principle over different orders.
